summary.text: A 20-year-old male presented to the emergency room one week after sudden visual impairment in the right eye with ocular pain. Brain CT showed no remarkable parenchymal abnormality, and intravenous methylprednisolone was started for optic neuritis. After an earlier outside MR showed T2 FLAIR hyperintensity, a comprehensive MRI was prompted to evaluate for multiple sclerosis.

One week after admission, left optic neuritis occurred and MRI showed demyelinating lesions at T4–T5, confirming multiple sclerosis. High-dose prednisolone 60 mg/day was tapered after five days with visual recovery. He had intermittent numbness and back pain without new lesions, was maintained on prednisolone 10 mg/day, and began multidisciplinary follow-up.

At 8 months after the MS diagnosis he developed sudden right-sided sensorineural hearing loss with an absent air-bone gap, the right average pure-tone threshold being 38.8 dB versus 13.8 dB on the left. Three intratympanic dexamethasone sessions were planned, and right-sided hearing completely recovered about one month after onset. Visual impairment also recurred and was treated with high-dose corticosteroids at another hospital.

About one month after right-sided recovery he presented with sudden bilateral hearing loss, with average thresholds of 55.0 dB right and 48.8 dB left. Intratympanic dexamethasone for each ear produced no significant change, and the corticosteroid dose was subsequently increased to 20 mg for an additional week with minimal pure-tone improvement. After observation without further treatment, hearing recovered substantially by three months after onset; ABR testing was not performed.

evidence.quote: At the time, the average pure-tone threshold for the right ear was significantly reduced to 38.8 dB, comparable to 13.8 dB for the left ear, indicative of a clear decrease, and it corresponded to sensorineural hearing loss without an air-bone gap.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not assign "At the time" or "three months after the onset" to the neighbouring SRT or SDS sentences.

ambiguities.issue: Discussion sentences about the literature (Cogan syndrome comparison, speech discrimination recovery pattern, systemic steroids as standard) are author interpretation or cited-series conclusions, not separate patient facts; the Cogan syndrome comparison is not a documented diagnosis or exclusion for this patient.

evidence.quote: Based on these points, it becomes possible to differentiate between MS and Cogan syndrome.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not record Cogan syndrome as ruled out or present for this patient.

article_limitations: Figure rows are caption-layer only (visual_status not_inspected); the three audiogram images were inspected in visual.json. Image-printed values (SRT and word recognition tables) are pixel content only and not facts.
The Figure 3 caption names oral methylprednisolone while the text names prednisolone; only the drug identity is quarantined (two review_only facts), the 20 mg one-week dose increase stays scored.
Literature tables (Tables 1 to 3) and discussion-level statistics describe other published patients and are not individual facts of this patient.
The first planned intratympanic dexamethasone course is not stated as delivered; time anchors "the onset" are kept literal.
